4098134.title: Yuseong On-Day
4098134.overview: A stay-and-relax program in Daejeon's Yuseong hot-spring district, built for slowing down rather than sightseeing. The lineup includes healing yoga classes combining aromatherapy and tea ceremony on the Kyeryong Spatel lawn, an open-air cinema with big screen and wireless headsets, small classical and film-music concerts in the front yard of Biryongjae — a former presidential villa — and an anytime running challenge along the Gapcheon stream. Participants get coupons usable at hotels, cafes, and bakeries in the hot-spring district. Schedules and sign-up at the official site (yu-on.com).
4098134.fee: See official website for program fees

4106883.title: COSMOS: BIGBANG 20th Anniversary Media Exhibition
4106883.overview: A media-art exhibition marking 20 years since BIGBANG's debut, staging two decades of the group's music and archives under the theme COSMOS. Held at dududo seoul, an underground venue between City Hall and Euljiro 1-ga stations, the show runs through a media tunnel, sound-visualization and listening zones, a media archive, an interactive art wall, a VR zone, and a hologram show, using AI, XR/VR, and 3D motion graphics. Entry is fully by advance reservation in 12 daily time slots, and the run is split into Phase 1 and Phase 2 with some contents and merch perks changing between phases. An MD zone operates on site.

3399432.title: 5th Jeju Biennale: The Art of Transformation
3399432.overview: Jeju's civilization arrived by sea and from the northern mainland alike — scattering, gathering, and transforming into the island's present-day ecology and way of life. The 5th Jeju Biennale takes that dynamic as its subject, borrowing its key concept 'Iyahong' from the refrain of a folk song that itself drifted in from the mainland and became native. Anchored at the Jeju Museum of Art with satellite venues including the Jeju Stone Park's Obaekjanggun Gallery (free with a biennale ticket), it presents an aesthetics of survival shaped by nature, human life, and the sacred.
3399432.place: Jeju Museum of Art and satellite venues
3399432.fee: Adults 8,000 won · Youth 4,000 won · Children 2,000 won (satellite venues free)

4096371.title: Treasure Hunter in Jinan
4096371.overview: A county-wide treasure hunt across seven zones of Jinan, a mountain county in Jeonbuk best known for the twin peaks of Maisan. Buy a pass, then visit sites like Maisan's northern zone, Tapsa Temple with its stone pagodas, Yongdam Dam, Jucheon Eco Park, the highland arboretum, the Bugwi metasequoia road, and Suseonru Pavilion, completing QR missions in the LocalVibe app. Hidden 'dragon orbs' are revealed zone by zone each Saturday — find a regular orb for on-site rewards, or a shining one to enter the finals. A clever excuse to actually cover the county's best spots.
4096371.place: Maisan north zone, Tapsa Temple, Yongdam Dam and other sites
4096371.fee: Early bird 2,000 won · Pre-registration 4,000 won · On-site 5,000 won

2748395.title: Nam-gu Youth Arts Festival
2748395.overview: Daegu's annual September showcase for young artists, returning with a two-part program: the small-venue 'Fringe FESTA' at the Daegu Music Creation Center (Sep 1–4) and the main-stage Youth Arts Festival at Daedeok Culture Center's Dream Hall (Sep 10–11). All seats are free, ages 5 and up. Alongside the performances, the 'ART CONNECT' exhibition brings together 104 young artists from regional art schools across painting, media, visual design, craft, and webtoons — free entry at Daedeok Culture Center galleries from Aug 18 to Sep 18 (closed Sundays).
2748395.place: Daedeok Culture Center and Daegu Music Creation Center

2648460.title: Gyeongbokgung Palace Starlight Tour
2648460.overview: A guided night program through the quieter northern grounds of Gyeongbokgung, Seoul's main royal palace, combining history and royal cuisine. With a specialist guide you move through the palace after dark, then sit down in the former royal kitchen for a modern reinterpretation of the Joseon royal table — a 12-dish surasang served dosirak-style. This year adds a changgeuk (Korean opera) performance inside Jibokjae, King Gojong's private library, before the evening closes at Hyangwonji Pond under the stars. One of the most sought-after tickets among the palace night programs — book early.
2648460.sponsor: Royal Palaces and Tombs Center, Korea Heritage Service

2640874.title: Seoul Light DDP Autumn
2640874.overview: The world's largest media-art projection on a freeform facade returns to Dongdaemun Design Plaza for 11 nights, September 3–13. Under the season theme DAYBREAKER, the autumn edition 'K-Original Light' traces the original lights behind today's Korean culture: a first-ever live performance stage with real-time responsive media art built on Nam June Paik's philosophy, media-art reinterpretations of painter Yoo Youngkuk and the Korean alphabet, and a finale combining light, sound, and lasers across Zaha Hadid's curved walls. Free, nightly 19:30–22:30.

4099532.title: Starry Sea Busan: Night Camp-nic at Dadaepo
4099532.overview: Dadaepo Beach Park — Busan's famous sunset spot — turns into an evening festival ground for three September weekends. The program runs from 'Sunset Eat-nic' picnic dining against the sunset, to the headline 'Night Music Camp-nic' of live music under camping lights, plus a dog-friendly 'Play Mung-nic' zone and wellness programs. Fridays and Saturdays, September 4–19, 17:00–22:00 across the beach park's three plazas. Live-show seating is ticketed; some free seating is available.
4099532.fee: Live shows: adults 13,000 won · children 5,000 won (some free seating)

4099101.title: Suwon Nammun Market Night Market 'Bulchwimugwi'
4099101.overview: 'No going home sober!' — King Jeongjo's famous toast lends its name to this night market at the Paldalmun gate markets in Suwon, held September 5 and 19. Built on the history of the market Jeongjo opened for his people, it fills the streets with food trucks, merchant stalls, and an art market, wrapped in a light story-world: duel the wandering taoist character, hunt hidden talismans, break magical seals. Eat, walk, and photograph your way through a market district that has been trading since the 18th century.
4099101.place: Paldalmun plaza and Jidonggyo Bridge area

4056606.title: House of the Upright Minister
4056606.overview: A family-friendly heritage program at the Chunghyeon Museum in Gwangmyeong, the head house of Yi Won-ik — one of Joseon's most celebrated 'clean officials', whose modest pavilion Gwangamdang was a gift from King Injo. The day mixes a participatory play about his life, mulberry natural-dye workshops, and a hanok exploration program for children, plus a free gayageum recital. Held four times: September 5 and 19, October 17, and November 7. Book via the official website; paid programs open Aug 10.
4056606.fee: Play 6,000 won · Hanok program 8,000 won · Natural dyeing 10,000 won · Combos 9,000–11,000 won · Gayageum recital free

617992.title: 16th Gwangju Biennale: You Must Change Your Life
617992.overview: Asia's most established contemporary art biennale opens September 5 under a title borrowed from the last line of Rilke's 1908 poem 'Archaic Torso of Apollo' — the moment a broken ancient statue upends how the viewer sees the world. The 16th edition builds on that jolt: when your vantage point shifts, you can no longer live as before. Held at the Gwangju Biennale Exhibition Hall, the event anchors Korea's contemporary art calendar and pairs well with the city's May 18 memorial sites and food scene.

3113583.title: Car-Free Jamsugyo Bridge Walking Festival
3113583.overview: On festival Sundays, Seoul closes Jamsugyo — the low double-deck bridge that skims the Han River at Banpo — to traffic and hands it to pedestrians. Regular attractions include the Moonlight Diner (global street food), the Moonlight Market for crafts and eco goods, and riverside rest zones, while each edition adds rotating specials like the 'Jamsugyo Water Wars' water-gun battle and the reimagined 'Moonlight Jamsugyo'. Free, 14:00–22:00, with the Banpo Rainbow Fountain nearby — one of the most pleasant free evenings in the city.
3113583.place: Jamsugyo Bridge and Banpo Hangang Park

2756253.title: Heritage Media Art at Buyeo Jeongnimsa Temple Site
2756253.overview: For three weeks, the UNESCO-listed Jeongnimsa Temple Site in Buyeo — heart of the ancient Baekje capital of Sabi — becomes a night media-art park. Projections on the five-story stone pagoda and lecture hall, laser art, large-screen displays, AI-based interactive pieces, and kinetic sculpture draw on Sabi-era motifs: the Great Gilt-bronze Incense Burner, lotus-pattern roof tiles, Baekje astronomy, craft, and architecture. Nightly 19:00–22:00, September 7–27, free. A rare chance to see one of Korea's most austere heritage sites in a completely different register.

4095402.title: Bookshelf Concert: Sherlock Holmes
4095402.overview: Gyeonggi Arts Center's signature chamber-music series reads literature through music — and the 2026 edition takes on Sherlock Holmes. Mystery novelist Jeong Myeong-seop hosts, unpacking Conan Doyle, the stories' Victorian backdrop, and their behind-the-scenes history, while a chamber ensemble scores the moods and scenes of the canon. No prior reading required; for Holmes devotees it is a fresh angle on a familiar world. A 90-minute evening for mystery fans, classical newcomers, and families alike. Note the talk is in Korean.

4075091.title: 2026 National e-Festival for Students with Disabilities
4075091.overview: A national esports and digital-skills festival for students with disabilities, co-hosted by the National Institute of Special Education, KOCCA, and the Netmarble Foundation under the theme 'A world opened by AI, boundless possibility'. Students selected through regional preliminaries in all 17 provinces compete in esports and IT contests, alongside AI and digital-technology experience programs, cultural performances, exhibition booths, and exchange programs at Sono Calm Vivaldi Park in Hongcheon.
4075091.sponsor: KOCCA · National Institute of Special Education · Netmarble Foundation

4093222.title: Gumi Local Food Festa in Seoul
4093222.overview: The city of Gumi brings its farm produce and G-Food brand to Seoul Plaza for a two-day showcase: sales booths direct from farms, a city promotion hall, an agri-food export fair, hands-on programs, and a produce auction visitors can join. A chance to browse regional Korean produce without leaving downtown Seoul.

2756396.title: Deoksugung Palace: Night at Seokjojeon Hall
2756396.overview: An evening at Seokjojeon, the neoclassical Western-style hall of the Korean Empire inside Deoksugung Palace. The program pairs a guided night tour of the hall with a terrace-cafe experience — coffee (gabae, the drink Emperor Gojong loved) and dessert over live classical music — and a musical performance telling the story of the imperial household. Running since 2021 and now a twice-yearly fixture, it closes with period-prop photos to take home. Around 100 minutes per session; tickets are limited and sell fast.
2756396.sponsor: Royal Palaces and Tombs Center, Korea Heritage Service

573459.title: 38th Chuncheon Puppet Festival
573459.overview: Asia's largest puppet-theater festival, drawing top puppeteers and companies from around the world to Chuncheon. Centered on the Chuncheon Puppet Theater but spilling across the city, the program spans international performances, a large-scale parade, an art market, and workshops, exhibitions, and hands-on programs that push the boundaries of the genre. Long a fixture of the world puppetry circuit, it is genuinely all-ages — as rewarding for adults as for children. Fees and times vary by program.
573459.place: Chuncheon Puppet Theater and citywide venues

2864606.title: 5th Horror Hologram Festival
2864606.overview: An immersive horror festival staged inside the Iksan Prison Set — the disused prison film set where many Korean movies were shot. The main event fuses hologram technology from Jeonbuk's hologram industry with escape-room mechanics and live theatrical scares, backed by stage events, quiz shows, and food stalls. Free entry, evenings 18:00–22:00 — a genuinely unusual venue even by horror-attraction standards, worth the detour for genre fans.
2864606.sponsor: Ministry of Science and ICT · Jeonbuk · Iksan City · NIPA

607417.title: Myeongnyang Daecheop Festival
607417.overview: A history festival commemorating the Battle of Myeongnyang (1597), when Admiral Yi Sun-sin's 13 ships defeated a vastly larger Japanese fleet in the roaring strait of Uldolmok. Jointly held by Jindo and Haenam counties on both shores of the actual strait, the festival's centerpiece is a multimedia naval-battle reenactment blending ICT effects with a marine parade, plus a departure parade, regional performances, nightscape lighting, and hands-on history programs. One of the most dramatic settings of any Korean festival — the tidal current that won the battle still races under the Jindo Bridge.
607417.place: Uldolmok Strait (Usuyeong, Haenam and Nokjin, Jindo)

3351888.title: Seocheon Heritage Night Tour
3351888.overview: A two-night heritage festival at Hansan Eupseong Fortress in Seocheon, themed 'The Lord of Hansan's Rowdy Incognito Outing'. The old fortress town — home of Korea's famous Hansan ramie fabric — hosts night performances, hands-on programs, and exhibitions that blend tradition with contemporary staging, September 11–12, 18:00–22:00, free. Part of Korea's national 'Heritage Night' series, which opens heritage sites after dark with food, light, and stories.

3499401.title: GXG 2026
3499401.overview: Korea's largest urban game-culture festival, held in Pangyo — the Silicon Valley of the Korean game industry. GXG (Game culture X Generation) treats games as culture rather than just play: the main program is GXG SOUND TRACK, a game-music competition, surrounded by concerts, exhibitions, and experience zones covering game music, video, and art. Free, on the plaza around Pangyo Station, 13:00–22:00 — an easy subway ride from Gangnam and a good window into Korean gaming culture.

2614762.title: Geoje Beer Festival
2614762.overview: Geoje Island's signature autumn festival: unlimited draft beer against the night sea of Jangseungpo Port. The waterfront park fills with local food and food trucks, while the stage cycles through EDM, K-pop, and retro hits with audience events between sets. The festival also runs tourism booths, photo zones, local makgeolli tastings, a barrier-free zone, and reusable-container operations. Ticketed entry; evenings 18:00–22:00.

2392105.title: Dalseong Daegu Contemporary Art Festival
2392105.overview: An open-air contemporary art festival at Gangjeong, by the sculptural ARC building on the Nakdong River. It inherits the spirit of the 1970s Daegu Contemporary Art Festival, when young artists challenged the rigidity of the art establishment — the 1977 edition at this very riverside drew some 200 artists in what is considered Korea's first collective art event. Free, open 11:00–22:00, and easy to combine with a riverside bike ride out of Daegu.

4095228.title: Namdo K-Garden Festival
4095228.overview: A 51-day night garden festival in Yeosu's old downtown under the theme 'A Night Garden Embracing Islands'. Around 40 gardens — showcase gardens, designer gardens, and citizen-made plots — line the Yeomun culture street and Yeoseo plaza, viewable day and night with evening lighting that ties into Yeosu's night-tourism circuit. Garden-interpretation walks, performances, and hands-on programs run throughout, 15:00–21:00, free. Runs September 11 to October 31, overlapping the city's peak autumn season.

3333149.title: Gwangmyeong Madanggeuk Festival
3333149.overview: A performing-arts festival devoted to madanggeuk — Korea's open-air folk theater of satire, humor, and audience participation — co-hosted with the national madanggeuk association. Now in its third year, it turns the Gwangmyeong Civic Stadium grounds into an open stage for madanggeuk, fusion gugak, circus, and street performance, with citizen-participation programs alongside. The form's defining trait is that the line between stage and audience disappears — expect to be pulled in. Free, 16:00–21:00.
3333149.sponsor: Gwangmyeong Cultural Foundation · Korea Madanggeuk Association

2826119.title: Chuncheon Sul Festa
2826119.overview: Chuncheon's traditional-liquor and local-food festival, celebrating the city's brewing culture. Local breweries pour takju, distilled soju, yakju, fruit wines, and craft beer for tasting, with bottles sold at fair prices, while local food brands and food trucks supply pairings. A busking stage and hands-on programs round out the evening at KT&G Sangsangmadang Chuncheon. Free entry; drinks purchased on site. An easy add-on to a Chuncheon day trip from Seoul on the ITX line.

3301271.title: Cheongsong White Porcelain Festival
3301271.overview: Cheongsong baekja — white porcelain fired here for 500 years from local clay, water, and fire — gets its own festival at the pottery village near Juwangsan National Park. Under the slogan '500 years of history, 500 years of future', the festival mixes exhibitions, sales, wheel-throwing and other hands-on programs, and cultural performances that trace the craft's past and hand it to the next generation. Free entry (some workshops paid), 10:00–19:00. Combine with Juwangsan's rock spires — this is one of Korea's quietest, prettiest counties.

4104786.title: Daejeon Jung-gu Heritage Night Tour
4104786.overview: A night festival threading together the modern-era heritage of Daejeon's original downtown — the former Chungcheongnam-do Provincial Office, Daeheung-dong Cathedral, and other early-20th-century buildings — with light installations, storytelling, performances, hands-on programs, and a night market through the old alleys. The point is to walk, listen, and participate rather than just look, discovering a district where the city's past and present coexist. Free (some programs paid), 18:00–22:00.

4106719.title: Moonlight Music Nights
4106719.overview: Open-air autumn concerts in everyday places — parks and streamsides across Daejeon's five districts, one evening per district from September to October. Local artists in classical, gugak, and band formats share the stage with popular guest singers, in venues like Gapcheon Eco Lake Park and Dongchundang Park. Free and unticketed: bring a mat, arrive at dusk, and take in a Korean city's ordinary evening at its best. 19:00–20:30.

1071143.title: Muchangpo Mystic Sea Road Festival
1071143.overview: Twice a month, the tide at Muchangpo Beach pulls back to expose a 1.5km sea road — and this Boryeong festival is timed to it. By day, walk the tidal flats when the sea parts, catch fish bare-handed, and watch open-air madanggeuk theater; after dark, the signature LED torch walk sends a line of lights out across the exposed seabed. A rare festival where the main event is a natural phenomenon, with the schedule set by the tide tables. Free entry; some programs paid.

3317667.title: Sinchon Global University Culture Festival
3317667.overview: Sinchon — Seoul's classic university district — fills Yonsei-ro with a festival built on its two identities: global culture and student culture. University students plan and run much of the program themselves: global culture-experience booths, world food stalls, and student-culture booths line the street, while the main stage cycles through student performances, global acts, and participatory events. Free, 11:00–21:00, and one of the easiest places to feel Korean campus energy without an invitation.

1409287.title: Samto Festival
1409287.overview: Wonju's harvest-season celebration of farming and rural culture. A direct farm market sells the region's produce at source prices, family programs cover rural crafts and games, and local arts groups fill the stage across the day. Less a tourist spectacle than a genuine regional fair — which is exactly its charm if you want to see how a Korean provincial city celebrates its farming roots. Free, 10:00–21:00 at the Wonju sports complex.

4098740.title: Dongdaemun-gu Book Festival
4098740.overview: A reading festival for Korea's September 'Month of Reading', themed 'Open the book, move the body!'. The plaza at the Dongdaemun-gu Office hosts reading fitness sessions, folk tales turned into physical games, and an open-air library, while the auditorium runs library-network booths from a reading adventure squad to a mini sports day and a 'reading health check'. Children's musicals, a bubble show, and busking round it out. Free, aimed squarely at families, 12:00–17:00.
4098740.place: Dongdaemun-gu Office Future Plaza and auditorium

3352029.title: Pocheon Hantangang Garden Festa
3352029.overview: A large-scale garden-and-ecology festival at the Hantangang Eco Landscape Complex, inside the UNESCO Global Geopark of the Hantan River gorge. Seasonal flower fields spread beneath the park's 410m Y-shaped suspension bridge, with themed designer gardens, a Pororo-themed autumn camping photo zone, a river market of Pocheon farm produce and street food, and family e-bike rides along the gorge. Ticketed entry, 09:00–18:00 (last entry 17:00). The geology alone — basalt cliffs carved by ancient lava — is worth the trip from Seoul.

3099365.title: Colorful Garden: Jaraseom Flower Festa
3099365.overview: Autumn flower fields blanket Jaraseom — the river island in Gapyeong best known for its jazz festival — from September 12 to October 5. Weekends add busking and local performances, plus balloon art and family programs, farm-produce booths, and snack stalls. Of the 7,000 won ticket, 5,000 won comes back as local currency to spend at booths and in town cafes and restaurants. Boats cruise the Bukhangang riverfront and an electric shuttle covers the walk in. Ticket holders get discounts at nearby attractions; Gapyeong residents enter free.
3099365.fee: 7,000 won (5,000 won returned as local currency)

2505657.title: Seoul Intangible Heritage Festival
2505657.overview: Seoul's intangible-heritage traditions gather in Namsangol Hanok Village for a weekend of performances, exhibitions, demonstrations, and tastings, organized into five themed courtyards: a spirited performance stage, a craft court where master artisans work within arm's reach, a taste court of traditional food and drink, an open participation court, and a heritage-collecting trail. Set among the village's relocated hanok houses under Namsan, it is one of the best-value traditional culture days in the city. Free (some programs paid).

1019773.title: Jeju Leisure Healing Festival
1019773.overview: Two days of leisure sports and wellness on Hamdeok Beach, one of Jeju's most beautiful white-sand bays. Headline concerts each evening (past lineups have drawn major Korean acts) bookend a daytime program of paddleboarding, flying disc, and trail running, balanced by wellness content: morning yoga on the sand, stargazing nights, and sketch-drawing sessions overlooking the water. Opens with a beach party performance and closes with a water-splash finale. Free, 07:00–22:00.

3000203.title: Yangju Heritage Night Tour
3000203.overview: The old government seat of Yangju-mok comes alive after dark under the theme 'Officials and people rejoicing together again'. The festival stages Yangju's remarkable roster of intangible heritage — the Byeolsandae mask dance, Sonori shamanic ox play, farming songs, and funeral bier songs — alongside a state-exam reenactment, traditional crafts, night walks, media exhibitions, and an old-style market with teahouse. Programs follow the classic '8 nights' structure of Korea's Heritage Night series (night views, night roads, night stories and more). Free, 17:00–22:00.

2034167.title: Pyeongtaek Lake Light Festival
2034167.overview: Pyeongtaek's signature festival on the shores of Pyeongtaek Lake, built around the twin themes of water and light. The day runs family performances, hands-on programs, and food zones through the lakeside tourist complex; after dark the sky fills with the festival's headline fireworks show over the water. Local residents and artists carry much of the stage program, making it a friendly, low-key alternative to the megafestivals. Free, 11:00–21:00.

3520705.title: Nowon Craft Beer Festival
3520705.overview: Thirty-four breweries from across Korea pour some 200 craft beers along the Gyeongchun Line Forest Trail at Hwarangdae Railroad Park — a disused rail line turned linear park in northeast Seoul. Traditional-market vendors and food trucks handle the pairings, while the stage hosts Korean and international acts in tandem with Seoul Music Week, plus experimental student art and children's programs. Free entry; pay per pour. One of the city's best-value beer events, in an unusually atmospheric venue.

3020552.title: Glocal Culture in Namsan Festival
3020552.overview: A one-day neighborhood festival in Busan's Geumjeong district where global and local culture meet — powered by the international students of Busan University of Foreign Studies and the residents of Namsan-dong. The glocal food market serves fermented dishes made by the community fermentation school alongside local staples, with a flea market of local sellers and an evening citizens' concert. Namsan-ro becomes a cultural street for the day, 15:00–22:00, free.

3494053.title: Paju K-Culture Festival
3494053.overview: A K-culture festival at the former Paju English Village — now a shooting location for K-pop survival shows, music videos, and K-dramas. The program brings K-pop and cover-dance performances together with K-food, traditional Korean games, and around 30 hands-on K-culture booths, plus four-cut photo studios, stamp events, and traditional costume try-ons. Free, 10:00–17:00. For K-content fans, the venue itself — a purpose-built European-style village an hour from Seoul — is half the draw.
3494053.place: Gyeonggi Future Education Paju Campus (former Paju English Village)

4098980.title: Wanju Sanggwan Water Pool Party
4098980.overview: A stay-style festival in Sanggwan, a valley township of Wanju county, linking its water, forests, hot springs, lodging, and food into one program. The daytime pool party and evening night market anchor the schedule, joined by cypress-forest activities ('Forest-tivity'), village and forest trekking walks, and lodging-linked stay packages. Free entry; the pool party and some programs are ticketed. Runs 10:00–22:00 at the Boem Spa & Resort area — an easy pairing with Jeonju, twenty minutes away.
4098980.fee: Free entry (pool party and some programs paid)
4098980.sponsor: Wanju County · Wanju Culture and Tourism Foundation

3303554.title: Cheoinseong Fortress Culture Festival
3303554.overview: In 1232, at the small earthen fortress of Cheoinseong, the monk-commander Kim Yun-hu and local villagers repelled the second Mongol invasion — killing the Mongol general Sartai in one of the great upsets of the era. Yongin's 35th festival in their honor stages a musical of the battle, mounted martial-arts shows, horseback riding, Goryeo costume try-ons, pottery and craft workshops, and guided history walks, closing with night performances and fireworks. Free entry, 10:00–22:00, with food trucks on site. A linked mission event connects it to October's Poeun Culture Festival.

4103259.title: 2026 DMZ Peace Festa
4103259.overview: A relay festival linking the tourism assets of the DMZ border region, long split between separate counties, into one program — this edition connecting Ganghwa Island and Cheorwon. Both legs build hands-on programs around three shared themes: nature and ecology, the lives and stories of border residents, and reflection and healing. Venues include the Hwagae Garden on Gyodong Island (Ganghwa) and the history park in Cheorwon. Free; some programs need advance booking via the official site.
4103259.place: Hwagae Garden, Gyodong Island (Ganghwa) and History Park (Cheorwon)
4103259.sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

4033328.title: 14th Busan International Port Conference
4033328.overview: The annual international conference of Busan Port — one of the world's busiest container hubs — gathering global port, shipping, and logistics leaders to share container-market outlooks and operating strategy. The 2026 agenda centers on the industry's defining shifts: digital transformation, decarbonization, and supply-chain realignment. Held at the Busan Port International Exhibition & Convention Center; free registration, with session times to be announced. An industry event rather than a festival — of interest mainly to maritime professionals.
4033328.place: Busan Port International Exhibition & Convention Center

2556687.title: Literature Week 2026: Sideways Glance
2556687.overview: Korea's national literature festival, held every year since 2016 to widen the audience for Korean writing. The 2026 edition, themed 'Sideways Glance', looks at literature and everything just outside it, over five days of readings, talks, and programs around Marronnier Park in Daehangno — Seoul's theater district. Free; program times vary. Most events are in Korean, but the park itself buzzes for the week.

2867141.title: 2026 Gyeongbuk K-Story Festival
2867141.overview: A content-industry festival in Andong themed 'K-Story, where content begins', connecting the region's history and its creators' stories to webtoons, video, performance, and publishing. The program spans story-IP pitching sessions that link creators with buyers, keynote lectures and conferences, family experience zones, and exhibitions and performances at the Andong Culture & Arts Center. Free, 11:00–20:00 — and Andong itself, Korea's Confucian heartland and home of Hahoe Village, rewards the trip.

734219.title: 39th Donghae Mureung Festival
734219.overview: Donghae's flagship traditional festival, four days at the Wellbeing Leports Town under the theme 'Citizens as one, Donghae leaping anew'. It opens with mountain-spirit and harvest rites, then runs generation-spanning concerts, a citizens' song contest, youth dance festival, navy band and honor-guard shows, special-forces martial-arts demonstrations, and folk performances including Mangsang nongak and the local bridge-treading play. Family zones cover folk games, craft workshops, and children's programs; a local-restaurant tasting vote and lantern-lit night tunnel round out the grounds. Free.
